subject.title: [Bug]: Teams Graph/media guarded fetches reject RFC2544-proxied hosts

question: Should the Teams plugin opt into RFC2544 only for concrete Microsoft Graph and configured media hostname allowlists while leaving wildcard or unscoped fetches strict?
rationale: This deliberately relaxes one SSRF classification for a proxy compatibility case, so maintainers must confirm the permanent trust boundary even though the proposed implementation is narrow.

options.title: Approve host-scoped exception
options.body: Permit RFC2544 only when a concrete Teams-owned hostname allowlist is also enforced, with negative tests for wildcard, non-Microsoft, and private-network targets.

options.title: Require live proxy proof first
options.body: Keep the proposed boundary but delay acceptance until a host-proxied container or equivalent real network run demonstrates the failure and fix.

options.title: Keep strict blocking
options.body: Reject the exception and document that RFC2544 fake-IP DNS environments are unsupported for Teams guarded fetches.

recommendation.title: Approve host-scoped exception
recommendation.body: Permit RFC2544 only when a concrete Teams-owned hostname allowlist is also enforced, with negative tests for wildcard, non-Microsoft, and private-network targets.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent DNS-pinning work is the closest feature-history ownership signal for the affected Teams media boundary.
